adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:113 — The lazy map refresh for newly deployed grants skips the duplicate-shortcut check from postInit and silently overwrites an existing shortcut mapping, so tokens decode to the wrong grant type.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType(), the lazy refresh path does `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` after looking up the new grant’s shortcut. If a newly deployed grant type uses a shortcut already assigned to an existing grant, this will overwrite the existing shortcut→grant mapping without any validation. The duplicate-shortcut validation only happens in postInit() (via the size comparison after initial population) and is not re-run on these incremental updates. This can cause `getGrantTypeByShortcut()` decoding to resolve the shortcut to the wrong grant type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:102 — grantType is captured from formParams only in the constructor, so setFormParams() leaves a stale grant type that then gets encoded into the token ID.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuth2GrantType.Context`, `grantType` is initialized once in the constructor via `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)` and exposed through `getGrantType()`, but `setFormParams(...)` (still present) does not update `grantType` accordingly. If any code path mutates the context by calling `setFormParams` after construction, `context.getGrantType()` can become inconsistent with the current `formParams`, and that stale value is then persisted into `ClientSessionContext` (`clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())` in `OAuth2GrantTypeBase`) and used for token-id encoding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Adding abstract getShortcut() with no default (and removing the Context copy constructor) breaks every third-party OAuth2GrantType implementation at compile or run time.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the public SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with no default implementation. In Java, this is source- and binary-incompatible: any third-party implementation not updated will fail to compile, and already-compiled implementations can throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime when Keycloak calls the new method (e.g., `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` now invokes `gtf.getShortcut()`). Separately, `OAuth2GrantType.Context`'s copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` is removed, which also breaks any external code relying on it. This is a concrete compatibility/API break shown by the diff, but not necessarily a logic defect in Keycloak itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — New abstract getShortcut() with no default method breaks every existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory (compile/AbstractMethodError), and a null shortcut NPEs in encoder factory postInit at startup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (server-spi-private/.../OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java). This is a source/binary incompatible change for any existing third-party implementations: recompilation will fail unless they implement it, and already-compiled implementations can throw `AbstractMethodError` when Keycloak calls `getShortcut()`. Additionally, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` unconditionally calls `gtf.getShortcut()` and puts it into `ConcurrentHashMap` (`grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName)` / `grantsToShortcuts.put(grantName, grantShortcut)`), which will throw an NPE if any factory returns `null` because `ConcurrentHashMap` does not permit null keys/values and there is no null validation in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1054 — Access token jti/event TOKEN_ID format changes from plain UUID to "xxxxxx:uuid" unconditionally, with no opt-out/compat flag or migration note for consumers that parse or store token ids.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes access token `jti` generation unconditionally: in `TokenManager.initToken` the ID is no longer `KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()` but `encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx)`, which produces a `6chars:rawId` format (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId`). There is no conditional/feature flag in the shown diff to preserve the prior plain-UUID `jti` format. Tests in `AssertEvents` were updated to expect the new structure, confirming the behavior change. This is a real compatibility concern for consumers that parse/store token IDs, but not a demonstrable correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — Decoder hardcodes 2-char grant shortcuts (context length 6) while the SPI javadoc advertises "3-letters" shortcuts and nothing validates length, so conforming custom grants produce undecodable token ids.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() assumes a fixed 6-char context and slices grant shortcut as exactly 2 chars (substring(4,6)), while OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() javadoc says shortcuts are “usually like 3-letters” and does not constrain length. encodeTokenId() concatenates the grant shortcut verbatim, so a custom grant with a 3+ char shortcut would produce an encoded ID that the decoder rejects (encodedContext.length() != 6) and there is no length validation in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() (it only checks for duplicate mappings). This is a real extensibility/correctness defect exposed by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:102 — Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed from the grant SPI without deprecation, breaking extensions that use it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor in `server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java` was removed entirely (it existed before and is deleted in the hunk starting around the `Context` constructors). Since this is part of a grant SPI type, removing a public constructor is a source/binary incompatible API change that can break external extensions compiled against it. The diff does not show any deprecation or compatibility shim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:82 — A custom grant whose shortcut collides with a built-in one fails server startup via IllegalStateException, making the new shortcut namespace a hard breaking constraint for existing extensions.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), grant shortcuts are collected into two maps (grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts) and then validated by comparing their sizes; if two OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations share the same shortcut, grantsByShortcuts will overwrite an entry while grantsToShortcuts (keyed by grant id) will not, causing the size mismatch and throwing an IllegalStateException, which would abort startup. This is a real, diff-grounded compatibility/design constraint for extensions, but it’s not inherently a correctness defect in the new logic—it's an intentional validation policy choice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — Public constructor documents rawTokenId as non-null but re-checks grantType instead, so null rawTokenId is accepted and yields "xxxxxx:null" ids.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added AccessTokenContext constructor, the null-check intended for rawTokenId is incorrectly written as `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. As a result, `rawTokenId` can be null without throwing, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` will concatenate it (`':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`), producing token IDs ending with ":null".

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:105 — grantType is cached from formParams in the constructor, and setFormParams never updates it, so the two can get out of sync

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuth2GrantType.Context`, `grantType` is initialized once in the constructor from `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`, but `setFormParams(...)` only updates `this.formParams` and never recomputes `this.grantType`. Since `getGrantType()` is later used (e.g., `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` sets `clientSessionCtx` attribute from `context.getGrantType()`), calling `setFormParams` can cause the cached `grantType` to diverge from the actual form params, producing an incorrect grant type in downstream logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — Test matcher re-hardcodes the token-id layout with wrong offsets (3,5 vs 4,6) and inverted equality, so it duplicates encoder format knowledge and cannot detect grant mismatches.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the grant shortcut extraction and comparison are incorrect. The encoder format in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider expects the context prefix to be 6 chars with grant shortcut at positions 4..6 (substring(4,6)), but the matcher uses substring(3,5), which targets the wrong two characters. Additionally, it inverts the check: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the expected shortcut and allows mismatches to pass if the raw part is a UUID. This makes the matcher unable to detect grant mismatches as intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:33 — Two unrelated "unknown" markers ("na" for grant vs "un" for enum UNKNOWN) and a grant-type sentinel stored in a String field create inconsistent, stringly-typed unknown handling.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows three different “unknown” representations across the token-id context: AccessTokenContext.SessionType.UNKNOWN and TokenType.UNKNOWN use shortcut "un" (AccessTokenContext enums), while DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider defines a separate UNKNOWN string sentinel "na" for grantType (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.UNKNOWN) and grantType itself is modeled as a raw String in AccessTokenContext. This is indeed inconsistent/stringly-typed, but the diff does not show a concrete broken behavior from it: the factory explicitly maps "na" <-> "na" in grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts, and getTokenContextFromTokenId/encodeTokenId handle it. So it’s a design/consistency concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:26 — Encoder in encode package depends on AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper just for a lightweight-token helper, which was widened from package-private to public static, leaking mapper internals.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider calling AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session) (new dependency from encode -> mappers) and AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper changing getShouldUseLightweightToken from package-private to `public static` to enable that call. This is a verifiable design/coupling concern introduced by the change (exposing a mapper helper more broadly), but it does not demonstrate a functional correctness bug by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:497 — Lazy map-refresh logic is duplicated between getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut and bypasses the duplicate-shortcut validation done in postInit.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, both getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() contain similar “refresh maps if missing” logic that updates grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts. This lazy refresh path does not re-run the duplicate-shortcut/duplicate-id validation performed in postInit (which only checks size equality after initial population). A newly deployed OAuth2GrantTypeFactory with a conflicting shortcut could be silently inserted/overwritten via ConcurrentHashMap.put, leading to ambiguous or incorrect mappings without triggering the postInit check. This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/edge-case concern, but it depends on misbehaving/duplicated extension grants at runtime rather than being an immediate defect in normal operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.java:134 — GRANT_TYPE attribute is set ad hoc in five different call sites (base class, ROPC, pre-auth, refresh, token exchange) with mixed sources, making coverage of new grants easy to miss.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows GRANT_TYPE being populated in multiple, separate places rather than centrally: OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse() sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE from context.getGrantType(); ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process() also sets it from context.getGrantType(); PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process() sets it from PreAuthorizedCodeGrantTypeFactory.GRANT_TYPE; TokenManager.validateToken() sets it to OAuth2Constants.REFRESH_TOKEN for refresh; StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient() sets it to OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE. Since TokenManager.initToken() now relies on Constants.GRANT_TYPE to encode the access token ID context, spreading this responsibility across disparate call sites makes it easy for new/other grant/token issuance paths to forget setting the attribute (falling back to UNKNOWN or potentially failing encoding for unexpected values). This is a maintainability/completeness concern grounded in the change, not a directly provable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/tokenexchange/StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:50 — Added import of TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory is unused.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `import org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory;` was added in `StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java`, and there is no reference to `TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory` anywhere in the shown changes (the code uses `OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE` instead). This is a verifiable unused-import nit, but not a functional defect evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/Constants.java:207 — Constants.GRANT_TYPE merely aliases OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE, adding a duplicate constant that call sites mix with OAuth2Constants.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `Constants.GRANT_TYPE = OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE`, so it is an alias. However, the finding frames this as a review problem (“duplicate constant” and “call sites mix”) without any verifiable defect or concrete negative impact shown in the diff. In fact, the diff consistently uses `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` as the *attribute key* when storing into `ClientSessionContext`, while `OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE` is used to read the request parameter; the “mixing” is intentional and not demonstrably problematic from the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory.java:40 — Grant shortcuts are inconsistently exposed: some factories define public GRANT_SHORTCUT constants while others return inline literals.

adjudication.rationale: The observation is factually true in the diff (e.g., AuthorizationCodeGrantTypeFactory/RefreshTokenGrantTypeFactory/CibaGrantTypeFactory/DeviceGrantTypeFactory introduce public GRANT_SHORTCUT constants, while ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory/PermissionGrantTypeFactory/TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory/ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantTypeFactory return inline literals like "cc"/"pg"/"te"/"ro"). However, this is an inconsistency/style/maintainability nit rather than a verifiable correctness defect or concrete functional issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:432 — grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts are package-private mutable fields unlike the other private maps, exposing internal state.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory`, `grantsByShortcuts` and `grantsToShortcuts` are declared without an access modifier (package-private) and are mutable (`ConcurrentHashMap`), while the other maps (`sessionTypesByShortcut`, `tokenTypesByShortcut`) are `private` and made unmodifiable after init. This is verifiable in the diff and does widen access to internal mutable state within the package (and is used directly by `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest`). It’s an encapsulation/maintainability concern rather than a concrete functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — New abstract getShortcut() has no default, so existing custom grant-type factories throw AbstractMethodError in encoder postInit and abort server startup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the public SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with no default implementation, and the new `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(...)` unconditionally calls `gtf.getShortcut()` for every discovered `OAuth2GrantType` factory. Any existing third-party/custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` compiled against the old interface will not have this method, and when Keycloak loads it and invokes `getShortcut()`, it will throw `AbstractMethodError`, causing `postInit` to fail and potentially abort startup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:75 — A grant factory returning a null shortcut causes ConcurrentHashMap.put NPE during postInit, failing startup with no clear error.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), it unconditionally does `String grantShortcut = gtf.getShortcut(); grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName);` using `ConcurrentHashMap`. `ConcurrentHashMap` rejects null keys/values and will throw a NullPointerException if any `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory#getShortcut()` (newly added to the interface) returns null, leading to startup failure without an explicit validation/error message in this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:113 — Lazy refresh paths insert new grant/shortcut pairs without the duplicate-shortcut check done in postInit, so a colliding hot-deployed grant silently overwrites mappings and mis-decodes token ids.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, postInit() builds grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts and validates uniqueness by comparing map sizes. However, the later “lazy refresh” paths (getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut()) mutate the same maps with put() without re-checking for duplicate shortcuts. In getShortcutByGrantType(), a newly discovered grant with a shortcut that collides with an existing one will overwrite grantsByShortcuts[shortcut] while still adding a new grantsToShortcuts[grantType], making the two maps inconsistent and potentially causing incorrect decoding/encoding of token IDs. This issue is directly grounded in the diff at the lazy refresh put() calls and the absence of any duplicate validation there.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — getTokenContextFromTokenId throws unchecked IllegalArgumentException on any externally supplied malformed jti containing ':' instead of degrading to UNKNOWN context, risking 500s for callers parsing untrusted tokens.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId(String), the method only degrades to UNKNOWN when no ':' is present. If a ':' is present but the prefix is malformed (encodedContext.length() != 6) or contains unknown shortcuts, it throws unchecked IllegalArgumentException. The diff does not show downstream callers or exception handling, so the claim about causing 500s for callers parsing untrusted tokens cannot be verified from this PR alone, but the behavior/robustness concern is real and directly grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1053 — Every access token issuance now throws IllegalStateException (500) if the grant type attribute is not a registered grant id, a hard failure where previously ids were always generated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a potential IllegalStateException when encoding the token id if the grant type cannot be mapped to a shortcut (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId() throws when factory.getShortcutByGrantType(...) returns null). However, it is not true that “every access token issuance now throws” when the grant type attribute is not registered: if the attribute is missing, getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() explicitly defaults it to UNKNOWN ("na"), and the factory maps UNKNOWN<->UNKNOWN in postInit(), so encoding still succeeds. Additionally, for normal token endpoint flows the grant type is taken from the request (OAuth2GrantType.Context sets grantType from formParams.getFirst(grant_type)) and all built-in grant factories in this diff implement getShortcut(), making them registered/mappable. The finding overstates the behavior as universal and ignores the UNKNOWN fallback shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:54 — getShouldUseLightweightToken dereferences session.getContext().getClient() for every token, so any token path without a context client now NPEs.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() the code calls AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session). That method (changed to public static in this diff) dereferences session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(...) without any null-check. Since the new token-id encoding path is invoked from TokenManager.initToken() for access token creation, any invocation where KeycloakSessionContext has no client set will now throw a NullPointerException.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — Null check validates grantType twice and never rawTokenId, so a null raw id produces a "...:null" token id.

adjudication.rationale: In `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the fourth null-check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. This means `rawTokenId` can be null without being rejected. Later, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, which would yield a token id ending with `:null` if `rawTokenId` is null.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:125 — Every unknown shortcut in a decoded token id triggers a full provider-factory stream scan with no negative caching, so malformed input can repeatedly force expensive lookups.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut(String), when a shortcut is not found in grantsByShortcuts, it triggers sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class) and scans/filter-matches shortcuts. If no factory matches, nothing is cached (grantsByShortcuts remains without that shortcut), so subsequent decodes with the same unknown shortcut will repeat the full stream scan each time. This is a real perf/DoS-hardening concern exposed by the diff, not a functional correctness break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:469 — Parsing an attacker-supplied token ID with an unknown grant shortcut triggers a full provider-factory scan on every call, since misses are never cached.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory#getGrantTypeByShortcut(String), when grantsByShortcuts.get(shortcut) returns null, the code runs sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class) to try to discover a matching shortcut and only caches on a hit. If the shortcut is unknown, no entry is added to grantsByShortcuts, so subsequent calls with the same unknown shortcut will repeat the full provider-factory stream scan every time. Since getTokenContextFromTokenId() parses the shortcut directly from the (potentially attacker-controlled) token ID and calls getGrantTypeByShortcut(), this creates a repeatable, input-triggered performance issue (potential DoS vector).

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:192 — rawTokenId null check validates grantType instead, so a null jti can be encoded as "xx:null" without failing.

adjudication.rationale: In the new AccessTokenContext constructor, the null checks are wrong: it calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of validating rawTokenId. As a result, rawTokenId can be null and encodeTokenId() will concatenate it ("...:" + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()), producing an encoded token id ending with ":null" without failing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — isAccessTokenId uses wrong offset substring(3,5) (grant is chars 4-6) and inverted logic (returns false on match), so the grant-type assertion never verifies the expected grant.
matched_golden_ids: In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same two problems as the golden comment: the grant shortcut substring uses the wrong indices (should be substring(4,6) for chars 4–5) and the match logic is inverted (returning false on equality), preventing proper grant-type verification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:482 — Matcher does not check prefix length before substring, so a short/legacy token id throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of a clean mismatch.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, after `String[] items = item.split(":")` and checking `items.length != 2`, the code immediately calls `items[0].substring(3, 5)` without verifying `items[0].length() >= 5`. For a short/legacy token id (e.g., prefix shorter than 5 chars but still containing a ':' so `items.length == 2`), this will throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of returning `false` (clean mismatch).

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:82 — testIncorrectGrantType catches any RuntimeException, and with null sessionFactory the "ac" lookup fails via NPE in the refresh path, so the test passes without exercising the intended IllegalArgumentException.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.testIncorrectGrantType, the test catches any RuntimeException and ignores it. In the test setup, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.sessionFactory is never set (provider constructed with factory that only had init() called), and grantsByShortcuts does not contain "ac". When parsing tokenId "ofrtac:5678", DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() calls factory.getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac"), which (on missing shortcut) dereferences sessionFactory (null) in the refresh path, causing an NPE. That NPE is a RuntimeException, so the test passes without actually asserting the intended IllegalArgumentException for unknown grant type. This is a real, diff-grounded issue but limited to the test (not a product/runtime defect).

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:42 — Test hand-populates factory maps instead of running postInit, leaving duplicate-shortcut validation and lazy grant-refresh paths untested.

adjudication.rationale: The new unit test’s setup bypasses the production initialization logic in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory. In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before(), it calls factory.init(null) and then directly assigns factory.grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts instead of exercising postInit(KeycloakSessionFactory), which is where grant shortcuts are discovered, duplicate-shortcut validation is performed (size check), and the lazy refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType()/getGrantTypeByShortcut() rely on sessionFactory. As written, the test only covers parsing/encoding given pre-populated maps, leaving the nontrivial factory wiring/validation and refresh behavior untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — No tests for malformed token ids (wrong prefix length, unknown session/token type shortcut, empty raw id, extra colons).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial parsing/validation logic in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() (e.g., enforcing encodedContext length==6, throwing on unknown session/token/grant shortcuts, splitting on ':'), but the newly added DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest only covers: a valid roundtrip, unknown grant shortcut, incorrect grant shortcut, and the legacy no-colon case. It does not cover other malformed inputs mentioned (wrong prefix length, unknown session/token type shortcut, empty raw id, extra colons), so the finding is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:45 — getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext (transient/offline/lightweight detection, null grant fallback) has no test coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial logic in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(): it derives SessionType from UserSessionModel persistence/offline state, TokenType from AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), and falls back to UNKNOWN when Constants.GRANT_TYPE is missing. The new unit test DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest only exercises getTokenContextFromTokenId() and encodeTokenId(), and does not cover getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() (no ClientSessionContext/UserSessionModel setup is present). This is a specific, diff-grounded missing test for newly added behavior, not an immediate functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1053 — Access token id format changes for all grants but no integration assertion covers password, client_credentials, token-exchange or pre-authorized grants (only ac/dg/rt/ci via the broken matcher).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes access token IDs to include a 6-char context prefix (sessionType+tokenType+grantShortcut) in TokenManager.initToken(). AssertEvents introduces isAccessTokenId(), but its logic is incorrect: it checks `items[0].substring(3, 5)` (should be the 2-char grant shortcut at positions 4..6) and it returns false when the shortcut equals the expected value (`if (...) return false;`), effectively accepting mismatched shortcuts. This makes the updated integration assertions unreliable/broken, and only a subset of flows (ac/dg/rt/ci) even attempt to assert the new format while other grant shortcuts added in the diff (cc/ro/te/pc/pg) are not covered here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — Null check for rawTokenId re-checks grantType, and no test covers null rawTokenId so the bug is uncaught.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the null-check intended for `rawTokenId` is incorrect: it calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId` (lines shown: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed");` followed by `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`). This means a null `rawTokenId` would not be rejected and could propagate, which is a real correctness defect introduced by the diff. The added test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest` does not include any case constructing `AccessTokenContext` with `rawTokenId == null`, so this bug would not be caught by tests in the diff.
